chemistry-killer-08.material: Di density of 20 % (mass percent) sodium hydroxide solution ($\mathrm{NaOH}$, formula mass 40) na 1.2 g/mL. If you wan dilute dis solution with water to make 600 mL of 0.5 M NaOH solution, wetin be di volume (mL) of 20 % NaOH solution wey you need? (Atomic masses H=1, O=16, Na=23. Molarity $M = \frac{10xd}{M_w}$, x na mass %, d na density of di solution in g/mL)
chemistry-killer-08.s.s1.prompt: Di density of 20 % (mass percent) sodium hydroxide solution ($\mathrm{NaOH}$, formula mass 40) na 1.2 g/mL. If you wan dilute dis solution with water to make 600 mL of 0.5 M NaOH solution, wetin be di volume (mL) of 20 % NaOH solution wey you need? (Atomic masses H=1, O=16, Na=23. Molarity $M = \frac{10xd}{M_w}$, x na mass %, d na density of di solution in g/mL)
chemistry-killer-08.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Molarity of 20 % NaOH $M = \frac{10 \times 20 \times 1.2}{40} = 6.0$ mol/L (inside 1 L = 1200 g of solution, NaOH na 240 g = 6 mol).
Step 2: Moles of solute for di solution wey dem wan make = 0.5 mol/L × 0.600 L = 0.30 mol (NaOH 12 g).
Step 3: For dilution di moles of solute dey constant: 6.0 × V = 0.30 → V = 0.050 L = 50 mL. (Check: 12 g ÷ 0.20 = 60 g of solution, 60 g ÷ 1.2 g/mL = 50 mL)
Answer: 50 mL (d). (Wrong answers: 60 mL na value wey dem calculate as M = 5.0 by ignoring di density, 72 mL na value wey dem multiply di 60 g by di density, and 5.0 mL na error for di decimal place)
